identityReview: Matched microprocessor engineer James B. (Jim) Keller through AMD, Intel and Tenstorrent biographies; distinct from other people named Jim Keller. Wikipedia gives American identity and ambiguous 1958/1959 birth. AMD age 53 in August 2012 and Intel age 59 in April 2018 do not establish an exact birth year. Kept birth null with birthUnknown true.
lifeStatusEvidence: October 19, 2026 Series E announcement quotes Jim Keller as CEO; current leadership page confirms CEO. November 16 company partnership is included as corporate activity, not a personal appearance or quote.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read official AMD biography, Intel appointment PDF and resignation release, Tenstorrent leadership and October/November releases, January 2021 issuer announcement via PR Newswire, January 2023 EE Times article, Wikipedia identity passage and Commons licensing/history. Targeted passages, not full product or financial audit.
sourceReview.scope: Education, cross-company processor work, appointments, resignation, CEO transition, financing and latest corporate partnership.
corrections: AMD confirms Penn State BS in electrical engineering. No verified graduation year adopted; no doctorate inferred.

AMD credits coauthorship of x86-64 and HyperTransport and team contributions to processors. Intel supports Apple A4/A5 and Zen leadership. No sole-inventor claim or attribution of all design/manufacturing to Keller.

P.A. Semi acquisition by Apple was in 2008, but this corporate date is not automatically his personal joining date; EE Times indicates he had left for Apple before the acquisition. Timeline states acquisition only.

Intel announced appointment April 26, 2018, with official start April 30. Role was senior vice president leading silicon engineering, after Tesla Autopilot and Low Voltage Hardware; not Intel CEO or CTO.

Intel June 11, 2020 resignation was effective that day. Release updated June 16; six-month consulting agreement is not continued executive tenure. Personal reasons is attributed to Intel, with no speculation about private causes.

Old evidence says Tenstorrent CTO since 2020 and Wikipedia says December 2020; issuer publicly announced president, CTO and board member on January 6, 2021. Timeline deliberately uses announcement date and does not claim no earlier relationship.

January 19, 2023 EE Times reports CEO/CTO role exchange with Ljubisa Bajic and prior investor relationship. Profile uses January 2023, does not label Keller original founder, and does not assume Bajic remains CTO today.

October 19, 2026 company release states Series E closed at $1.5 billion and $6.2 billion post-money valuation. Neither is revenue, personal wealth or independently audited cash evidence. Promotional performance claims omitted.

November 16, 2026 partnership reports platform validation and planned joint sales. No claim of completed global deployment, independent benchmark verification or Keller personally conducting validation. Company release quotes Grant Jensen, not Keller.
Birth-year ambiguity retained. Reuters June 2026 acquisition talks search result is not evidence that Qualcomm completed an acquisition; no sale asserted.
sourceReview.limits: AI authored and reviewed, not human/native-language certified. Current employer assertions are attributed; no independent hardware benchmarking or full financial audit.
